_notes: The Walking Dead (v1.56, 2014, Stern).
Stern SAM platform. ARM AT91 CPU, NVRAM at CPU 0x02100000.
Scores are 4-byte little-endian integers.
Score entry: 4-byte score at start, initials (+0x08 bytes) as null-terminated ch.
Stride between entries is 0x20 bytes.
Verified against NVRAM data with real scores.
game_state was measured on twd_156c, a colour-hack revision, and twd_156c added to roms after
this map's existing sections were validated against its NVRAM byte for byte: every champion and
high score reads sensible initials and round default thresholds, and Last Man Standing Champion
reads 75,000,000, matching what the machine displayed at game over. The CPU RAM addresses below
were only measured on twd_156c; if plain twd_156 ever disagrees, game_state is the part to split.
Scores are 4 bytes on 4-byte centres from 0x021109E4, verified against the exit dump as
557,270 / 909,500 / 745,750 / 178,880. Stride 8 runs into the 0xFFFFFFFF fill.
current_player/current_ball came from the joint pair test, which reported two candidates here.
The exit dump separated them: 0x000329B4 reads player 4 / ball 3, the true end state, while
0x00031C2C reads 243 / 2 and is not a counter pair at all. The pair test narrows sharply but is
not always unique, so the exit dump stays part of the procedure.
Free Play was not toggled on this game. Its address is derived, and the derivation is worth
stating because it is testable rather than assumed. Machine adjustments are an array of 8-byte
records from 0x02102008 -- a 32-bit little-endian value, then a byte holding 0xFF minus the sum
of the value's four bytes, padded 0xFF above. Every record in every image checked satisfies it.
Aligning this game's array against a game where Free Play was measured puts it at one of only
two positions across all twenty SAM games examined, and the value there reads 1 on a cabinet
that is in free play. The alignment was validated prospectively: on nba_802 and smanve_101 --
the two games where alignment agreement was weakest -- the address was predicted first, then
confirmed by toggling, and both were exact.
Writing this field requires updating its check byte, or the game discards the change on reload.
The check byte is declared with an explicit checksum address. Without one, a checksum8
record means the checksum occupies the tail of start..end, which is not this layout: here
the summed bytes and the check byte are separate fields of one record.
ball_count and max_credits are derived, not measured on this game: on every Stern SAM game
measured they sit three and one records below free_play in the adjustment array, a rule
confirmed by menu changes with distinctive values on both array layouts (st_162h and trn_174h).
At the derived addresses this game's image reads the factory defaults, 3 balls and 30 credits,
with valid check bytes. Writing either field requires updating its check byte.
game_over, credits and volume come from a 1,098-frame recording of live memory on twd_156c,
spanning an operator-menu session and a full game with a tilt on ball 1. The session also
promoted ball_count and max_credits from derived to measured: menu values 5 and 9 landed at
adjustment indices 30 and 32 as the free_play-relative rule predicted. As with game_state, these
were measured on twd_156c only.
This ROM does not keep the ball+0x31 status byte its siblings use (a constant 0 here).
game_over at 0x00035E48 is a latch: 0 through the operator menu and the game, 1 from nineteen
samples after the last score change (the end-of-ball bonus) through attract. Correct in all
1,098 frames. It reads 0 before the first game of a session, so it is not a general 'no game in
progress' flag; it is exact for end-of-game detection.
volume at 0x02110250, set from 40 to 42 in the operator menu: the byte followed 40, 41, 42 and
the check byte after it followed 215, 214, 213 -- 0xFF minus the value -- declared as checksum8.
Note the Master Volume address is not shared platform-wide: nba_802 keeps it at 0x0211024C.
credits at 0x0211100C, the fifteenth SAM game at that address.
tilted is deliberately absent. The tilt on ball 1 froze scoring from f167 to the drain at f180,
and no byte in the 64KB state block holds one value through that window and another through
normal play. The one lead, 0x00038A24, read 2 at ball start, 1 in play, 0 from the tilt to the
ball end -- then latched at 2 for balls 2 to 5 and the attract, so it is a ball-1 state the
tilt cancelled rather than a repeatable flag, and it is not declared.
